title: IP-MT288-EditorAgentContextAttach

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build the Antigravity / Cursor 'Add to context' seam — the editor-side path that lets an operator attach a code/notes selection, a whole file, or a symbol to the bound agent session's prompt context as a typed, removable context chip (Cursor Ctrl+L 'Add to Chat', @-mentions of files/symbols). The MT-281 matrix marks 'agent-editor-context-attach' MISSING: interop/interaction_bus.rs carries clipboard + shared selection only; there is NO path that turns an editor selection/file/symbol into structured agent-session context feeding the WP-017 session API (MT-007). This MT owns the typed ContextItem model, the 'attach' commands in both editors, and the removable context-chip strip; the CONSUMER is an agent session (MT-007 AgentSessionService: the attached context rides the launch initial_prompt / steer payload). It does NOT build prompts, does NOT call a model, and does NOT own the chat dock (MT-098) — it produces structured context the session consumes.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) NEW module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/agent_context.rs (typed AgentContextItem + AgentContextSet + the attach/remove API + serialization to the MT-007 session context payload); (b) `pub mod agent_context;` (or re-export) in interop/mod.rs; (c) a NEW context-chip strip widget src/frontend/handshake_native/src/agent_context_bar.rs (the removable chips UI, mountable beside the chat dock / worksurface); (d) attach entry points: a code-editor command 'Add Selection to Agent Context' + 'Add File' + 'Add Symbol' in code_editor (via the existing command/context-menu surfaces) and the rich-editor equivalent for a block/selection; (e) one integration test file. Consumes MT-007 (session context payload); reuses the interaction_bus selection + code_nav symbol + the existing context-menu infra; NO backend model code.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. agent_context.rs: `pub enum AgentContextItem { Selection { pane_id, surface (code|rich), file_path: Option<String>, start: usize, end: usize, text: String, language: Option<String> }, File { path: String, byte_len: usize }, Symbol { file_path: String, symbol_name: String, kind: String, range: (usize,usize) }, Block { block_id: String, doc_id: String } }`; `pub struct AgentContextSet { items: Vec<AgentContextItem>, max_items: usize (cap, RISK), total_bytes: usize (running budget) }`. `attach(item)` dedups (same file/selection/symbol added twice is one chip) and enforces the item + byte cap; `remove(idx)`; `to_session_context() -> SessionContextPayload` serializes to the MT-007 launch/steer context shape (a typed list, NOT a rendered prompt string — the session owns rendering).
2. Attach sources: code editor — the primary selection (reuse interop interaction_bus SharedSelection / CodeEditorPanel::selected_primary_text), the open file, or the symbol under the caret (reuse code_nav symbol resolution + the MT-283 breadcrumb leaf / outline). Rich editor — the current selection text or a whole block (reuse the rich interop_adapter block_ref_selection). Each attach is a command wired through the existing command_registry / context_menu_surfaces (the same Copy/Copy-as-note-reference precedent), NOT a new ad-hoc menu system.
3. Context-chip strip (agent_context_bar.rs): a horizontal strip of removable chips, each showing an icon + label ('sel: foo.rs:10-24', 'file: bar.rs', '#symbol', 'block: …') + an 'x' remove button, plus a 'Clear all' and a live 'N items • ~K tokens' budget readout (bytes as a proxy; exact tokenization is the model's job). Chips are the operator's explicit, visible, removable control over what the agent sees (no hidden context). Colors/icons from theme tokens.
4. Budget + safety (binding): the set enforces a max item count and a byte budget; attaching past the budget shows a visible 'context full — remove an item' state rather than silently dropping or truncating. A stale chip (its file/selection no longer exists or the selection range drifted) is marked stale in the strip and excluded from to_session_context() until refreshed — the agent is never sent a phantom range. Nothing is auto-attached; every item is an explicit operator action (no silent context capture).
5. Handoff to the session: to_session_context() feeds the MT-007 launch initial context and the steer path (so 'add to context then steer' works). MT-287 (inline AI edit) reuses this set as its Ctrl+K context payload when present. The payload is a typed structure; this MT does NOT concatenate a prompt.
6. AccessKit: the strip is a Role::Group `agent_context_bar` (instance-suffixed), each chip a Role::ListItem `agent_context_chip_{n}` with a remove Role::Button `agent_context_chip_{n}_remove`, and a `agent_context_clear_all` button.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read interop/interaction_bus.rs (SharedSelection, selection publishing, the clipboard command precedent), interop/mod.rs (adapter registration), code_editor/panel.rs selected_primary_text + code_nav symbol resolution, rich_editor interop_adapter (block_ref_selection, text_selection), command_registry.rs + context_menu_surfaces.rs (how existing editor commands/menu items are registered — reuse for the attach commands), and the WP-017 MT-007 contract (the session context payload field on launch/steer).
2. Create interop/agent_context.rs with AgentContextItem/AgentContextSet + attach/remove/dedup/budget + to_session_context() serialization to the MT-007 shape; unit-test dedup, budget enforcement, and stale exclusion.
3. Create agent_context_bar.rs (the removable chip strip + budget readout + AccessKit nodes); unit-test the chip render model + remove/clear.
4. Wire the attach commands into command_registry / context_menu_surfaces for code (selection/file/symbol) and rich (selection/block); wire to_session_context() into the MT-007 launch/steer call site (or a typed seam if the chat dock host owns the call).
5. Register the modules; integration test: attach a code selection, a file, and a symbol -> three deduped chips + budget readout; remove one; over-budget shows the full state; a drifted selection chip is marked stale and excluded from to_session_context(); the serialized payload matches the MT-007 context shape. Capture Argus screenshot + AccessKit tree of the chip strip with mixed item kinds and the over-budget state.
6. Update the UserManual (same change): Add to Agent Context — the commands, the chip strip, removing/clearing, the budget readout, stale chips, and that nothing is sent to the agent that is not a visible chip.
forbidden_paths: src/backend/** (the agent session runtime is MT-007; this MT produces context it consumes, no backend model code)
src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/inline_ai/** (MT-287 owns the inline-edit seam; it CONSUMES this context set, do not modify it here)
acceptance_criteria: interop/agent_context.rs exists with AgentContextItem{Selection,File,Symbol,Block} + AgentContextSet (attach/remove/dedup, item + byte budget) + to_session_context() serializing to the MT-007 session context payload as a TYPED list (not a rendered prompt string).

Attach commands exist for the code editor (selection / file / symbol) and the rich editor (selection / block), wired through the existing command_registry / context_menu_surfaces (not a new ad-hoc menu), reusing interaction_bus selection + code_nav symbol + rich interop_adapter.

agent_context_bar.rs renders a removable chip strip with per-chip labels + remove buttons, a Clear-all, and a live 'N items • ~K tokens/bytes' budget readout; colors/icons from theme tokens (no hardcoded hex).

Budget is enforced: attaching past the item/byte cap shows a visible 'context full' state, never silently drops or truncates; a stale chip (missing file / drifted selection) is marked stale and EXCLUDED from to_session_context() (no phantom range sent).
Nothing is auto-attached: every context item is an explicit operator action, and everything the agent receives corresponds to a visible chip (no hidden context).
to_session_context() feeds the MT-007 launch/steer context; the payload shape matches the MT-007 contract (grep/test-provable); no model call or prompt concatenation in this MT.
AccessKit author_ids agent_context_bar / agent_context_chip_{n} / agent_context_chip_{n}_remove / agent_context_clear_all are stable and instance-suffixed.
UserManual updated in the same change: attach commands, chip strip, remove/clear, budget readout, stale chips, no-hidden-context guarantee.
proof_targets: Argus evidence: argus.screenshot + AccessKit tree of the context-chip strip with a selection + file + symbol chip and the over-budget state, stored under $HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT
expected_tests: unit: attach dedups an identical selection/file/symbol into one chip
unit: item + byte budget enforced; over-budget attach yields the 'context full' state, never a silent drop
unit: stale item (missing file / drifted range) marked stale and excluded from to_session_context()
unit: to_session_context() serializes to the MT-007 context payload shape (typed list, not a prompt string)
unit: AccessKit chip-strip node tree (bar + chips + remove + clear-all, stable suffixed ids)
integration: attach code selection + file + symbol -> three chips + budget readout; remove one; clear all
integration: rich-editor block attach produces a Block chip
implementation_notes: Verified grounding 2026-07-21: interop/interaction_bus.rs carries SharedSelection + clipboard commands only (no agent-context path); code_editor/panel.rs selected_primary_text + code_nav symbol resolution supply code context; rich_editor interop_adapter (block_ref_selection/text_selection) supplies rich context; command_registry.rs + context_menu_surfaces.rs are the existing command/menu registration surfaces (Copy / Copy-as-note-reference precedent) to reuse. WP-017 MT-007 launch/steer DTOs carry the session context this set serializes into.

Design basis (cite in code docs): Cursor 'Add to Chat' (Ctrl+L) + @-mention of files/symbols; Antigravity context attachment — explicit, visible, removable context chips with a budget readout; nothing hidden.
NO-HIDDEN-CONTEXT is load-bearing: everything the agent receives must correspond to a visible chip and an explicit operator action. The set never auto-captures the open file or selection.

This MT produces a TYPED context structure, not a prompt. The agent session (MT-007) renders it. MT-287 reuses this set for Ctrl+K inline-edit context; MT-098 chat dock is the conversational host that may display the strip.
Cross-family seams (reference only): MT-007 session API (consumer), MT-287 inline AI edit (reuses the set), MT-098 chat dock (host surface), MT-283 breadcrumb leaf (symbol source).

surfaces: attach commands / context-menu items in both editors

target_entries: Add to Agent Context: the attach commands (selection/file/symbol/block), the removable chip strip, remove/clear, the budget readout, stale chips, and the guarantee that nothing reaches the agent that is not a visible chip

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Attaching context is a local UI action; the session consuming the context (MT-007) owns the steer/launch events that carry it.
The context set (items, budget usage, stale flags) is exposed as structured state so a no-context model can see exactly what the agent will receive and why an item was excluded.
UI + typed-data surface; no child process.

risk_if_missed: The native editor cannot feed a selection, file, or symbol into an agent session as structured, visible context — the Cursor/Antigravity 'add to chat / @-mention' affordance — so operators must paste code manually (lossy, no provenance) and the inline-AI edit seam (MT-287) has no rich context source.

risks: RISK-1: Hidden context — the open file or selection is auto-attached without an explicit action, so the agent silently receives content the operator did not choose to share.
RISK-2: Phantom range — a stale/drifted selection chip is sent to the agent pointing at code that moved or was deleted, giving the model wrong context.
RISK-3: Budget blowout — attaching a huge file silently truncates or floods the session context, degrading the agent or exceeding limits with no operator signal.
RISK-4: Prompt coupling — the set concatenates a prompt string instead of a typed list, coupling the editor to a specific model's prompt format and violating the model/editor separation.
RISK-5: AccessKit collision — chip ids collide across mounts, breaking the Argus/keyboard remove path.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Every item is an explicit operator command; a test asserts the set is empty until an attach command runs and that the open file is not auto-added.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Stale/drifted items are marked stale and excluded from to_session_context(); a test drifts a selection and asserts it is excluded from the payload.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Item + byte budget enforced with a visible 'context full' state; a test attaches past the cap and asserts no silent drop/truncation.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): to_session_context() returns a typed list matching the MT-007 shape; a grep proof asserts no prompt-template/model-endpoint code and a test asserts the typed structure, not a concatenated string.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Chips use instance-suffixed author_ids; a dual-mount test asserts non-colliding ids and a working remove path.
